summary.text: Yes, if an approved dependant does not have enough MediSave. Sign the form at the hospital.

details.heading: There is a withdrawal limit
details.body: The amount they can use is subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits for each hospitalisation episode.

details.heading: Any balance is paid in cash
details.body: If the hospital bill is still not fully paid after the withdrawal limit, the remaining amount must be paid in cash.

steps.name: Check the family member
steps.text: Make sure they are your spouse, child, parent, grandparent or sibling. Grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

steps.name: Sign the hospital form
steps.text: Go to the hospital where your family member is receiving treatment and sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form.

sources.page_title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my family member’s hospitalisation expenses?

quotes.text: If your approved dependants do not have sufficient MediSave for their hospitalisation expenses, you may consider using your MediSave to pay for them.

Approved dependants refer to a member’s spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. They can be of any nationality except for grandparents and siblings who must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

Should you wish to use your MediSave for your approved dependants’ hospitalisation expenses, you may approach the hospital where they are receiving treatment at to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF).

It is important to note that while your approved dependants can tap on your MediSave, the amount they can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis.
If they still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after using up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, they would have to pay the remainder in cash.
